lines.text: A customer writes: “I paid, here's my screenshot.” Free OCR with rules grabs two hundred eighty-eight thousand won: the card bill. Nemotron picks the payment to the shop. And the payment ledger has never seen it. The date was edited.
Here it is live. First a real payment: a card text message, in Korean.
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, on Nebius Token Factory, reads the photo: the payment, not the running total, not the ad, not the phone's clock.
The ledger confirms it: same amount, within ten minutes. The money chain shows the one link where the money got stuck.
Nemotron can't spot an edit. It finds which number to check, and the ledger proves it: no payment at that time. The reply politely asks for the card statement.

On sixteen held-out phone photos made by a separate agent, Nemotron read the payment right and reached the right verdict on fourteen. Free OCR with rules, three. Reading the image, Nemotron got all eight edited ones, and the ledger rejected every one.
Messages are messy too. Two addresses: the account is his wife's, but he paid with his own.
Nemotron 3.5 Lightning reads the message: who is writing, what they claim, which records to look up. Addresses are masked before the model sees them, and anything the message doesn't say is dropped.
A simple rule would grab the first address and find nothing.
A verifier, not the model, walks the chain. The order was saved under a typo, exmaple dot com, and the mail bounced.
Every call is on screen: which Nemotron did which job, the time, the tokens and the cost. Ultra re-reads when the first reading is unsure, which on Korean threads was most of the time.
Approve, and the fix runs. On the public demo, only your own copy of the data changes.
Ask for someone else's order, and it is not read. And when nothing was charged, it says so. Nothing is broken. You were never charged.

On twenty-two Korean-heavy messages, Nemotron found who was writing in twenty; rules alone, sixteen. End to end, rules got one more right. One of Nemotron's misses was an attack where it named no sender, so nobody's records were read.
Paid, but nothing arrived? Now you can show the customer where the money stopped. NVIDIA Nemotron, on Nebius Token Factory.
